title: Rectangular beam
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees around the x-axis, zero degrees around the y-axis, and negative ninety degrees around the z-axis. Ensure the translation vector is set to zero in all directions. On the first face, draw the first loop consisting of four lines. Start the first line from the origin at (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0536, 0.0). Continue with the second line from (0.0536, 0.0) to (0.0536, 0.125). Draw the third line from (0.0536, 0.125) to (0.0, 0.125), and finish with the fourth line from (0.0, 0.125) back to the origin. Apply a scaling factor of 0.125 to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles as the coordinate system and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the transformed sketch to a depth of 0.75 units along the normal direction, ensuring no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction. Perform a boolean operation to create a new solid body from this extrusion. The final dimensions of the rectangular beam are length: 0.053571428571428575 units, width: 0.125 units, and height: 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0536, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0536, 0.125) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.125) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
